# ggcolonviz

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of ggcolonviz is to provide a ggplot2 extension for visualizing the colon, and with the `"ibd"` variant the whole gastrointestinal tract, in a clear and informative way. It is designed for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) data: segment scores, Montreal disease location, lesions, and changes over time.


## Installation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Sanofi-Public/ggcolonviz")
```

## Quick start

See which segments exist, then colour them with your own per-segment data:

```{r map, fig.height = 7, out.width = "50%"}
library(ggcolonviz)

colon_map("ibd")
```

```{r quick-start, fig.height = 7, out.width = "50%"}
scores <- data.frame(
  part = c("Terminal ileum", "Cecum", "Ascending", "Transverse",
           "Descending", "Sigmoid", "Rectum", "Perianal"),
  score = c(3, 2, 1, 0, 0, 1, 2, 1)
)

colon_plot(scores, fill = score, variant = "ibd")
```

`colon_parts()` lists the valid segment names, `montreal_parts()` translates
Montreal codes (L1-L4, p, E1-E3) into segments, and `colon_position()` places
lesions on a segment. See `vignette("IBD", package = "ggcolonviz")` for a
step-by-step guide.

## Building plots layer by layer

For full control, use the `geom_colon()` and `geom_colon_label()` layers directly:

```{r example}
library(ggcolonviz)
library(ggplot2)

patient_data <- data.frame(
  x = 0,
  y = 0,
  part = c(
    "Ileum",
    "Cecum",
    "Sigmoid",
    "Ascending",
    "Descending",
    "Transverse",
    "Rectum"
  )
)

patient_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, part = part)) +
  geom_colon(
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.5,
    fill = "lightblue"
  ) +
  geom_colon_label() +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_void()

```
